title: Validation run: streaming stability and external-function-call correctness across newly onboarded model variants
creator: Myles Carter
description: Objective: Provide a repeatable verification workflow that asserts newly onboarded model variants meet Redwood streaming semantics and external function/tool call correctness before the model is published with a streaming-capable performance profile. This ticket covers both functional correctness (message framing, function-call JSON schema, backpressure behavior) and non-functional characteristics (end-to-end tail latency under continuous streaming, stable chunk ordering, KV-cache interaction during tool invocations).
acceptance_criteria: A gating test suite executes against each model variant and returns PASS for all streaming+tool scenarios before the model is marked 'streaming-supported' in the model catalog.
Published performance profile for streaming endpoints includes median and p95 per-token latency, average tool-invoke latency, and throughput at three recommended batch sizes.
No undetected silent failures: the harness must detect dropped tool-call payloads, misordered streamed chunks, or missing function signature metadata.

Version-pinning workflow documents how a serving config references an exact model snapshot and associated runtime-compatibility tag; the onboarding checklist must include a pointer to the passed streaming/tool-call test run ID.
Smoke regression runs in CI that simulate failure modes (slow upstream tool, partial chunk loss, sudden KV-cache eviction) are green and provide triage logs to S3/console traces.
Test results and performance metrics are exported into the 'runtime-2.3' profile format and surfaced on the onboarding dashboard for reviewers.
steps: Inventory target model variants for this onboarding batch and annotate expected streaming semantics in Model Metadata (chunking strategy, max_chunk_tokens, supports_fn_calls:true/false)
Extend existing streaming harness to add tool-call middlewares: validate function-call start/end markers, JSON schema conformance, and idempotency markers for retries
Create synthetic tool stubs that emulate realistic latencies and error modes (400/500, timeouts, partial responses) behind an HTTP/gRPC boundary
Run baseline perf sweep across three sequence lengths and three batch sizes; collect per-token latency histograms and tool-invoke latency distributions
Run chaos scenarios: inject delayed tool responses, drop 1% of stream frames, and evict KV cache entries mid-conversation; collect failure rates and recovery traces
Capture logs/traces and convert into the performance profile YAML/JSON schema used by the model catalog publisher
Open review PR describing passing criteria and attach test run artifacts; request sign-off from Runtime QA and Model Onboarding PM
notes: This ticket intentionally separates functional conformance (message framing, fn-call payload integrity) from perf profile thresholds. Both must pass but have independent gating steps.
Prefer black-box harnesses that exercise the public API layer rather than instrumenting internal kernel paths to ensure compatibility with Dedicated and Private deployments.
Keep an eye on how quantized variants behave under streaming: small changes in chunk emission timing can amplify downstream tool-call timeouts.

We will publish a short 'Known limitations' section for models that stream but have degraded tool-call fidelity at high concurrency. These models can be marked as 'streaming-limited' until mitigations land.
